segments.text: Jupiter is the giant of our solar system. More than a thousand Earths could fit inside it.
segments.headline: 1,000+ Earths fit inside

segments.text: And yet, a day here lasts only about ten hours. It's the fastest spinning planet in the solar system.
There's no ground to stand on. Jupiter is a ball of gas, mostly hydrogen and helium, getting hotter and denser the deeper you fall.
segments.headline: No surface at all

segments.text: See that red spot? It's a storm bigger than Earth, and it has been raging for at least a hundred and fifty years.
segments.headline: A storm bigger than Earth

segments.text: Jupiter also has more than a hundred moons.
One of them, Europa, hides a salty ocean under its ice. It may hold twice as much water as all of Earth's oceans.
segments.headline: An ocean under the ice

segments.text: Tomorrow, we visit the jewel of the solar system. Next stop: Saturn, a planet light enough to float in water. Follow, so you don't miss episode five.
